signal_explanation: Lower bit rate increases settling/setup margin but does not automatically change signal amplitude, GPIO edge slew or external interference. Ringing/false clock edges, level translation, loading and power transients may remain at slow bit rates. Faster transfer reduces elapsed capture time while reducing timing margin. No SNR/waveform measurement exists for this setup.
evidence_priority: Reference-image mismatch alone may reflect changed contents or unresolved bank identity. Same physical address yielding different immediate readouts/read sizes is the stronger acquisition inconsistency. Targeted100kHzpair differed4072/4096bytes;50kHzpair matched each other but not prior100kHzfirst or larger-read slice.
source_audit_findings: Upstreamflashrom1.6linux_spi uses mode0,8-bit transfers, SPI_MASTER_4BA and SPI_IOC_MESSAGE(2) for command plus read data.
MT25QU256 definition includesFEATURE_4BA_WREN; macro includes native4-byte read support. spi_nbyte_read selects native4-byte read opcode when chip and programmer support it.
This makes a simplistic assumed3-byte/4-byte mismatch unproven; actual runtime command/CS/chunk behavior still requires independent validation.
Upstreamsource review does not prove exact installed package binary equivalence or identify a software defect.
working_hypotheses: Electrical: translation/drive/loading/clock edge or supply behavior despite mechanical continuity
Transaction: command/address sampling, chip-select boundaries, chunk/read-order/state or implementation behavior
Current image/bank/reference differences: explain reference mismatch, not same-address read inconsistency by themselves
next_refinement: Pause additional clip changes while completing read-transaction/chunk/address audit; then choose one independent same-address fixed-small-block read implementation and controlled speed comparison. Earlier short-clip reversal remains a possible control, not a proven clip fault. No new hardware test, flash repair or write selected this turn.
